A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of genetic variants found to reside in cis with a known deleterious mutation can be excluded as fully penetrance mutations.
the vast majority of genetic variants found by clinical testing of BRCA 1 are likely to have no or low penetrance for breast and ovarian cancer.
the clinical significance of a genetic variant found in trans with a deleterious mutation is likely to be reduced risk for cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic testing can be performed on a large scale, and variants can be classified as being likely benign or likely pathogenic based upon their location in the context of known deleterious alleles.
the clinical significance of variants of uncertain clinical signifcance can be determined in trans with deleterious mutations in the same gene, and this is especially relevant for BRCA1 and BRCA2.
genetic variants detected in trans with known pathogenic variants should be considered as being of reduced clinical significance.
